title: 2005 AMC 10A Problem 10
statement: There are two values of \(a\) for which the equation \(4x^2 + ax + 8x + 9 = 0\) has only one solution for \(x.\) What is the sum of those values of \(a?\)

solutions.text:
Writing the equation as \(4x^2 + (a+8)x + 9 = 0,\) there is one solution exactly when the discriminant \((a+8)^2 - 144 = 0.\) Then \(a + 8 = \pm 12,\) so \(a = 4\) or \(a = -20,\) and their sum is \(-16.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: A quadratic has exactly one solution when its discriminant equals \(0\)
Combine the linear terms into \((a + 8)x,\) then set \((a+8)^2 - 4 \cdot 4 \cdot 9 = 0\)
